extracted.intended_audience: K08 career-development applicants, mentors, and NIH reviewers in infectious disease/human immunology
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and presentation of an NIH K08 mentored career-development research proposal in infectious diseases focused on antibody Fc-mediated mechanisms against Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including specific aims, preliminary data, experimental approach, and career training plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate background and rationale for career development
rubrics_metrics.description: The candidate must demonstrate relevant prior clinical and research experience (global health rotations, residency, infectious diseases fellowship, prior NIH T32 support), specific exposure to the disease area (e.g., MDR-TB in Haiti, teaching in Tanzania), and a clear motivation for pursuing the proposed subspecialty and research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how prior experiences shaped research interests; list completed and in-progress coursework (e.g., immunology, biostatistics, programming, microscopy); cite presentations and manuscripts in review; argue that K08 funding is critical for transition to independence from scientific and leadership perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear long-term career goals and five-year training plan
rubrics_metrics.description: State explicit career-development goals for the next five years (e.g., elucidate antibody Fc effector mechanisms and identify Mtb antigens that elicit functional antibodies) and justify the need for additional training in specific techniques and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify coursework and lab skills to be acquired (antibody effector function analysis, cell biology, microscopy, data analysis) and link these to the candidate's prior skills and the project's feasibility and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims structure and hypothesis-driven framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a succinct overall hypothesis and 2–4 specific aims, each with a clear hypothesis and experimental approach tied to the central question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be testable and logically connected to the scientific objective (e.g., Aim 1: define antigen specificity; Aim 2: dissect Fc/FcR-mediated intracellular restriction; Aim 3: identify macrophage effector mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance — articulate the problem, gap, and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the public-health burden (e.g., one in three people carry TB), the limitations of current understanding or tools (lack of effective diagnostics and vaccines), and why the proposed work addresses a critical gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight how better mechanistic understanding could inform diagnostics, correlates of protection, therapeutics, or vaccine design; discuss limitations of existing models (mouse models do not recapitulate latency/granulomas) to justify human-focused work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation — define novelty relative to field
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state how the proposal challenges existing paradigms (e.g., shifting focus from Ab titres/neutralization to Fc-mediated effector functions, glycosylation and subclass effects) and why this is a novel approach in TB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe novel methods, conceptual advances, or unique combinations (systems serology, human sera and human infection models) that increase chance of breakthrough findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data supporting feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Include and interpret preliminary results that directly support each aim (e.g., systems serology showing different humoral signatures in LTB vs ATB; in vitro macrophage assays where LTB IgG mediates greater bacterial restriction; affinity differences for FcγRIIIa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preliminary data to justify approaches, sample sizes, and likelihood of success; show technical competence in assays and analysis; present representative figures and key statistical outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach — detailed experimental design and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concrete experimental methods for each aim (e.g., Mtb proteome arrays, IgG purification and depletion, ADCC/ADCP assays, capillary electrophoresis for glycan profiling, high-throughput fluorescence microscopy and CellProfiler image analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe reagents, instruments (GenePix scanner), analysis software (GenePix Pro, CellProfiler), infection models (primary human monocyte-derived macrophages infected with H37Rv-MCherry), time courses (96 hrs), MOI, and how outcomes (bacterial burden) will be quantified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort design, sample size, and generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Define source populations, cohort sizes, and rationale for numbers (e.g., LTB n=34 and ATB n=34 for array probing), and plan to validate findings in an independent, age-matched cohort to assess generalizability and control for confounders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss collaboration arrangements for specimen access and how cohort selection addresses potential hidden confounders (age, geography).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and computational analysis plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate analytic methods (e.g., multivariate feature reduction to identify candidate immune correlates) and report statistical tests with p-values (Student t test, Mann–Whitney, Wilcoxon), and metrics for functional assays (MFI, percent frequency, phagocytic score).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify how features from high-dimensional assays will be reduced and validated; indicate thresholds for significance and measures to assess reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional validation criteria for candidate antigens
rubrics_metrics.description: Define explicit criteria for calling an antigen 'of interest': depletion of antigen-specific IgG decreases ADCC; ADCC in response to that antigen is greater than for others; antigen-specific IgG display glycosylation patterns associated with functionality (e.g., increased bisecting GlcNAC, decreased fucose, increased galactose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan sequential validation: (1) depletion of antigen-specific IgG from bulk IgG and test ADCC, (2) side-by-side ADCC comparisons with bulk IgG against identified antigens, (3) glycan profiling of antigen-specific IgG using capillary electrophoresis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of complementary orthogonal approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine different technical strategies (proteome arrays, antigen-specific depletion, monoclonal antibodies, glycan profiling, enzymatic manipulation of antibodies, microscopy) to converge on mechanistic conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: antigen-specific titres are often low, so using multiple complementary methods increases confidence in functional assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causal interrogation of Fc/FcR function
rubrics_metrics.description: Design experiments to test causality between Fc/FcR interactions and intracellular Mtb fate (e.g., IdeS cleavage to separate Fc from Fab, PNGase deglycosylation, F(ab)2 and Fc fraction testing, siRNA knockdown of FcγRIIIa, localization/clustering assays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate controls (e.g., FcγRIIb knockdown), and interpret possible outcomes (loss of function after enzymatic manipulation indicates Fc dependence; unchanged function suggests Fc-independent mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis-driven receptor-level testing (FcγRIIIa focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: If preliminary data implicate a specific receptor (here FcγRIIIa), propose targeted experiments: assess affinity differences (e.g., SPR), visualize receptor clustering and colocalization with labeled IgG, and perform receptor-specific knockdown to test impact on bacterial restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and define predicted results (e.g., knockdown of FcγRIIIa but not FcγRIIb should abrogate LTB IgG-driven restriction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanistic aim to identify macrophage effector pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline plans to identify intracellular effector mechanisms by which antibodies influence bacterial fate (e.g., enhanced phagolysosomal fusion, inflammasome activation and IL1β secretion) and include kinetic analyses to parse temporal relationships among processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify assays to measure these processes and how they link to functional outcomes (bacterial burden), and plan to identify 'drivers' within intertwined processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected outcomes and alternative interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experimental approach, articulate expected results and alternative scenarios (e.g., multiple antigens act collaboratively, Fc modifications alone change functionality, antibody effects are antigen-nonspecific or mediated via cytokine neutralization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe how each possible outcome will be interpreted and what follow-up experiments or analyses would distinguish alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential pitfalls and alternative strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify likely technical or conceptual pitfalls (e.g., antigen arrays miss glycolipid antigens; siRNA transfection may activate macrophages) and provide feasible alternative strategies (e.g., glycan arrays for glycolipid epitopes; use THP-1 cell line for gene manipulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate anticipation of problems and readiness with contingency plans to preserve project progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of human-relevant models and translational emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize use of human sera and human cell-based infection models to maximize physiological relevance and facilitate targeted translation into animal models only when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify departures from standard animal models (mice do not recapitulate latency/granulomas) and link human-focused results to potential implications for diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment, mentorship, and institutional support
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the training environment and mentorship (e.g., combined training at Massachusetts General Hospital and Brigham and Women’s Hospital; mentors Sarah Fortune and Galit Alter; Boston TB research community) and explain how it supports career development and project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate access to necessary expertise, resources, and collaborative networks to accomplish the aims and transition to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and reporting of quantitative results
rubrics_metrics.description: Report quantitative assay outcomes with appropriate summary statistics (mean ± SEM), replicate numbers, and statistical tests (report p-values), and use high-throughput, quantitative readouts (e.g., pixel per macrophage quantitation via CellProfiler).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear figure legends, define metrics (e.g., phagocytic score calculated by MFI and percent frequency), and ensure reproducible data processing pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation in independent cohorts and control for confounders
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to validate identified correlates/features in an independent cohort (e.g., Texas cohort age-matched to South African cohort) to address potential confounders and assess generalizability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use replication across geographically and demographically distinct cohorts; consider power/sample-size recalculation based on pilot results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of antigen candidate groups and prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify detected antigens into meaningful groups (antigens recognized by both LTB and ATB; antigens recognized only by LTB; antigens recognized only by ATB) and prioritize LTB-specific antigens as most likely to elicit protective Fc signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a small subset of antigens to be differentially recognized; plan combined depletion testing of candidate sets as an initial broad validation step.
